technical_and_design_decisions: Use existing Spring Cloud Data Flow module registration pattern for adding the HDFS sink module, ensuring compatibility with the streaming pipeline architecture.
Implement Hadoop shell commands using the Spring Shell framework, leveraging existing command patterns for consistency.
For composed jobs repository, utilize a database-backed repository (e.g., JPA) to persist job definitions, following Spring Data patterns.
Orchestration of composed jobs will be implemented as a state machine or a sequential/parallel workflow runner using Spring Batch or custom job execution logic.
Test coverage for shell commands will be achieved by mocking Hadoop filesystem interactions and using Spring Shell's test utilities for isolated command testing.
Message binding via expressions will leverage Spring Expression Language (SpEL) integrated into the Spring Cloud Stream binder, allowing dynamic routing and transformation.
Moving JDBC and Kafka modules from XD to s-c-s will involve copying source code, adjusting package names and dependencies, and ensuring backward compatibility with existing configurations.
assumptions: The developer is experienced with the Spring ecosystem, including Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Shell, and related projects.

No major architectural changes are required; all tasks are incremental additions or migrations within the existing frameworks.
Effort estimates include design, coding, unit testing, integration testing, documentation, and code review for each user story.
The developer works full-time on this increment with no significant interruptions.

activities.activity_name: Add HDFS sink to module registry
activities.activity_description: Design and implement a new HDFS sink module for Spring Cloud Data Flow, register it in the module registry, and provide integration tests to ensure it can write to Hadoop filesystem in a streaming pipeline.

activities.activity_name: Add support for Hadoop commands in shell
activities.activity_description: Implement shell commands (e.g., ls, put, get) using Spring Shell to interact with Hadoop filesystem, including command parsing and integration with Hadoop client APIs.

activities.activity_name: Explore repository options for composed jobs
activities.activity_description: Research and implement a repository for reading and writing composed job definitions, likely using Spring Data JPA with a relational database, and integrate it into the composed job management system.
Design and implement the orchestration logic for composed jobs, allowing users to define and execute multiple jobs in a single workflow, supporting sequential and parallel execution.

activities.activity_name: Add test coverage for shell commands in isolation
activities.activity_description: Develop unit tests for shell commands by mocking Hadoop interactions and using Spring Shell's test framework, enabling isolated command testing without full end-to-end deployment.

activities.activity_name: Support XD-like message binding with expressions
activities.activity_description: Extend Spring Cloud Stream binder to allow module binding via SpEL expressions on incoming messages, enabling dynamic property binding for microservice modules.

activities.activity_name: Move JDBC module from XD to s-c-s
activities.activity_description: Migrate the JDBC sink module from the XD codebase to the Spring Cloud Stream repository, updating dependencies and ensuring it works as a sink in streaming pipelines.

activities.activity_name: Move Kafka module from XD to s-c-s
activities.activity_description: Migrate the Kafka source module from the XD codebase to the Spring Cloud Stream repository, adjusting for the new repository structure and ensuring compatibility.
